cards.front: What is the formula for the Fourier coefficient c_k of a periodic signal?
cards.back: c_k = (1/T) * integral over one period of x(t) e^{-j k w0 t} dt
cards.source: Atlas/Academic/SEM 1 Modules/5CCYB020 Signals and Systems/Week 4/Signals and Systems Week 4 tutor.md

cards.front: State Parseval's theorem for a periodic signal.
cards.back: The mean power (1/T) integral |x(t)|^2 dt equals the sum of |c_k|^2 over all k.
cards.source: Atlas/Academic/SEM 1 Modules/5CCYB020 Signals and Systems/Week 4/Signals and Systems Week 4 tutor.md

cards.front: A square wave is approximated by more and more harmonics. What happens to the overshoot at the jump?
cards.back: It stays at about 9% of the jump (the Gibbs phenomenon); it gets narrower, not smaller.
cards.source: Atlas/Academic/SEM 1 Modules/5CCYB020 Signals and Systems/Week 4/Signals and Systems Week 4 tutor.md

cards.front: Write the convolution integral for an LTI system with impulse response h(t).
cards.back: y(t) = integral of x(tau) h(t - tau) dtau over all tau
cards.source: Atlas/Academic/SEM 1 Modules/5CCYB020 Signals and Systems/Week 4/Signals and Systems Week 4 tutor.md

cards.front: Convolve a rectangular pulse of width 1 with itself. What shape is the result, and how wide?
cards.back: A triangle, of width 2: the overlap grows linearly then shrinks.
